summary: Record the submitting incarnation on immutable work.submitted receipts and expose it in work reads.

replay.detail: Legacy work.submitted claims remain admissible and replay with an unknown submitting incarnation. An older member retains new-field claims as waiting unknown-claim-field records in the original signed envelopes; startup admission and canonical projection replay learn them after upgrade. The signed isolated mixed-registry regression checks log parity before upgrade and graph/table parity after upgrade.

schema.detail: No SQLite schema migration, new table/index, or stored-claim rewrite. The optional submitted_incarnation field changes the claim registry digest, and the optional work response field changes the generated client contract digest.

rules.detail: Claim vocabulary digest changes; checkpoint rules version is unchanged. Mixed registries continue exchanging signed envelopes and known claims but suspend projection equality checks. An older member cannot project new submissions carrying submitted_incarnation until upgraded.

compatibility.detail: Optional work.submitted field and work-read field. Tested registry pair: current registry with submitted_incarnation versus the same registry with that field removed. Missing/null incarnation means unknown and never validates a match. Lease claimant/claim_incarnation still clear on complete; missing-work-incarnation and wrong-work-incarnation fencing is unchanged. Rust, Swift and TypeScript clients are regenerated.

downtime.detail: Normal process restart is required. Restart-to-API and restart-to-health durations on production stores have not been measured; an older member with waiting submissions also needs admission and canonical projection recovery.

manual.detail: Upgrade all members that evaluate work completion before depending on incarnation-bound submissions. During rolling upgrade, inspect replication waiting_claims and do not treat a missing incarnation as a match. Let upgraded members admit and project their waiting claims before requiring projection parity.

recovery.detail: Roll forward an older member to learn retained submissions. No database migration needs reversal. An actual binary downgrade of a store already admitting this field has not been tested; use the reviewed previous-binary/store snapshot recovery procedure rather than assuming older readers prove new submissions. The mixed-registry regression covers waiting claims before upgrade and their canonical admission after upgrade.
